This patch sorts out an asymmetry in deletions. Currently
deletion commands come with an implicit content flush on deletion.

column2: chain deletion results in -EBUSY if there is content in this
so no implicit flush happens. So you have to send a flush command

column1: in first place to delete chains
column2: this is inconsistent and it can be

column1: annoying in terms of user experience.
This patch uses the new NLM_F_NONREC flag to request non-recursive chain

column2: ie. if the chain to be removed contains rules

column1: returns EBUSY. This problem was discussed during the NFWS'17 in Faro

column2: you hit -EBUSY if you try to delete a chain that
so you have to flush first before you can remove

column1: anything. Since iptables-compat uses the nf_tables netlink interface
has to use the NLM_F_NONREC flag from userspace to retain the original

column2: ie.  bail out on removing chains that contain rules.
